articles.title: Navigating the 4-Quadrant NLE Studio
articles.goal: Understand the four quadrants of the Sovereign Video Studio—Asset Dock, 60fps Centre Player, Inspector Panel, and Multi-Track Timeline—so you can edit efficiently.
prerequisites: An active studio session on FamilyPlatform (/family-studio) or PartyPlatform (/video-studio/[eventId]).
steps: 1. Locate the Top Bar to switch aspect ratios (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), Undo/Redo edits, open ? How to Use, or trigger Export 4K Master.
2. Use the Top-Left Asset Dock to browse Media, Overlays, Audio, Text, Stickers, Effects, Transitions, Captions, Filters, Adjustment, Charts & PiP, Templates, and AI Avatars.
3. Preview your composition in real time on the Centre 60fps Player (#snleMainCanvas) and drag golden handles to resize or rotate selected layers.
4. Fine-tune clip properties in the Right-Hand Inspector Panel across Basic, Remove BG, Mask, Retouch, Speed, Animation, Tracking, Adjustment, Lighting, and Audio tabs.
5. Arrange, split, and trim clips on the Bottom Multi-Track Timeline using the toolbar and scrub bar.
articles.expected_result: You can move fluidly between asset selection, live canvas manipulation, inspector tuning, and timeline sequencing without leaving the single-screen workspace.

common_issues.issue: Panels stack vertically on smaller screens.
common_issues.resolution: Below 1180px viewport width, the 4-quadrant grid automatically stacks into a single-column responsive layout for comfortable mobile and tablet editing.

example_use_cases: Launching the Interactive Spotlight Tour on your first visit to learn every panel in under a minute.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Full 4-quadrant Sovereign NLE Studio workspace showing Top Bar, Asset Dock, Centre 60fps Canvas, Inspector Panel, and Multi-Track Timeline]

articles.title: Uploading Media via the Direct R2 Vault & Media Dock
articles.goal: Upload video clips, photos, and audio straight to your Direct R2 Vault and place them onto the NLE timeline.
prerequisites: A supported media file (MP4, WebM, MOV, JPEG, PNG, or MP3/WAV).
A valid studio vault token (automatically provisioned when you open the studio).
steps: 1. Select your source video or photo in the studio upload panel to stream it directly to the Direct R2 Vault without overloading the web server.
2. Open the Media tab in the Top-Left Asset Dock.
3. Click + Add Video Clip (V1) or + Add Overlay Clip (V2) to place media onto the corresponding timeline track.
4. Confirm the new clip block appears on the Multi-Track Timeline and renders in the Centre 60fps Player.
articles.expected_result: Your media is securely stored in the Direct R2 Vault and immediately available as an editable clip on the timeline.

common_issues.issue: Upload stalls or returns a 403/401 error.
common_issues.resolution: Refresh the page to renew your CSRF and vault tokens, then retry the Direct R2 upload.

example_use_cases: Importing wedding speeches or family reunion clips directly from your phone into the R2 Vault.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Direct R2 Vault uploader and Media dock tab with + Add Video Clip (V1) button highlighted]

articles.title: Choosing Your Format: 16:9, 1:1, and 9:16 Aspect Ratios
articles.goal: Optimise your canvas dimensions for widescreen television (16:9), square feeds (1:1), or vertical Reels and Stories (9:16).
prerequisites: The studio viewport (#fvsViewportWrap) and 4-Quadrant NLE Studio loaded.
steps: 1. In the studio viewport header ([data-fvs-aspect]) or the NLE Top Bar, click 16:9 (1920 × 1080), 1:1 (1080 × 1080), or 9:16 (1080 × 1920).
2. Observe the live canvas (#snleMainCanvas) and viewport wrapper immediately resize to the selected aspect ratio.
3. Use the Inspector Basic controls or drag the canvas handles to re-centre subjects within the new frame.
articles.expected_result: Both the studio viewport and the NLE engine canvas synchronise to the chosen resolution and aspect ratio.

common_issues.issue: Edges of a 16:9 video appear cropped when switching to 9:16.
common_issues.resolution: Select the clip and adjust Position X/Y or Scale in the Basic Inspector tab, or click ▭ Crop 16:9 to reset safe framing.

example_use_cases: Publishing a 9:16 vertical highlight Reel for mobile guests while keeping a 16:9 widescreen master for family archives.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Format switcher buttons 16:9, 1:1, 9:16 and #fvsViewportWrap resizing live]

articles.title: Splitting, Duplicating (Alt+Click), and Stretching (+2s) Clips
articles.goal: Divide a clip at the playhead, clone clips rapidly, or extend clip duration by 2 seconds.
prerequisites: At least one clip placed and selected on the Multi-Track Timeline.
steps: 1. Scrub the timeline playhead to the exact frame where you want to make a cut.
2. Click ✂ Split on the timeline toolbar to divide the selected clip into two independent segments.
3. To clone a clip, click ⧉ Duplicate on the toolbar—or hold Alt and click (Alt+Click) directly on any clip.
4. To lengthen a still or title clip, select it and click +2s Stretch to add 2.0 seconds to its duration.
articles.expected_result: Clips split cleanly at the playhead, duplicates appear immediately, and stretched clips extend by 2.0s.

common_issues.resolution: Ensure a clip is actively selected and the playhead sits inside the clip's start-to-end range (not at the very edge).

example_use_cases: Trimming out a shaky camera intro by splitting at 00:00:03:00 and deleting the opening segment.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Multi-Track Timeline toolbar highlighting ✂ Split, ⧉ Duplicate, and +2s Stretch]

articles.title: Ripple Delete & Magnetic Snap Alignment
articles.goal: Remove unwanted clips without leaving black gaps and align clips cleanly with Magnetic Snap.
prerequisites: Two or more clips arranged on a timeline track.
steps: 1. Select the unwanted clip on the timeline.
2. Click 🗑 Ripple Delete in the timeline toolbar.
3. Notice that all subsequent clips on the same track automatically shift left to close the gap.
4. Toggle 🧲 Snap: On / Off in the toolbar to enable or disable magnetic snapping when dragging clips near playheads or neighbouring clip edges.
articles.expected_result: Deleted clips leave zero dead air, and Magnetic Snap locks neighbouring clips flush together.

common_issues.issue: Clips overlap slightly when dragged manually.
common_issues.resolution: Verify 🧲 Snap: On is active in the timeline toolbar so clip boundaries snap cleanly.

example_use_cases: Removing a 4-second pause in the middle of a birthday toast without manually dragging ten downstream clips.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Timeline showing 🗑 Ripple Delete and 🧲 Snap: On buttons]

articles.title: Freeze Frame, Reverse, Mirror & Crop 16:9
articles.goal: Create dramatic still moments, reverse playback direction, mirror footage horizontally, or apply a 16:9 safe crop.
prerequisites: A selected clip on the timeline.
steps: 1. Position the playhead over the moment you want to hold and click ❄ Freeze Frame to insert a still segment.
2. Click ⇄ Reverse to toggle backward playback on the selected clip.
3. Click ⇆ Mirror to flip the clip horizontally (ideal for correcting mirrored selfie camera footage).
4. Click ▭ Crop 16:9 to apply a 16:9 safe-frame crop to the selected clip.
articles.expected_result: The Centre 60fps Player immediately reflects the freeze, reverse, horizontal mirror, or 16:9 crop.

common_issues.issue: Reversed text in a front-facing camera recording.
common_issues.resolution: Select the clip and click ⇆ Mirror once to restore readable left-to-right orientation.

example_use_cases: Freezing the exact moment confetti bursts, or mirroring a front-camera greeting so venue signage reads correctly.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Timeline toolbar showing ❄ Freeze Frame, ⇄ Reverse, ⇆ Mirror, and ▭ Crop 16:9]

articles.title: Undo/Redo History, Track Controls & Sequential V1 Merging
articles.goal: Safely experiment with Undo/Redo, manage stacked tracks (+ Track, Mute/Lock), and understand how sequential V1 clips merge on export.
prerequisites: An active studio session with one or more timeline tracks.
steps: 1. Click Undo or Redo in the Top Bar at any time to step backward or forward through your in-session edit history.
2. Click + Track on the timeline toolbar to add stacked video tracks (e.g. V2, V3) for picture-in-picture or layered overlays.
3. Use each track's Mute or Lock toggle on the left track header to silence audio or prevent accidental drags.
4. Place multiple clips sequentially on V1: during playback and Export 4K Master, sequential clips on V1 merge automatically in timeline order.
5. Note that Undo/Redo and track edits manage your live in-session project; always export your 4K Master before closing the browser tab.
articles.expected_result: You can iterate fearlessly with Undo/Redo, isolate tracks cleanly, and merge sequential V1 clips into one continuous film on export.

common_issues.issue: Closing or refreshing the browser clears unsaved in-session timeline edits.
common_issues.resolution: Click Export 4K Master (or Publish Reel) once your edit is complete, as timeline state is managed in-session.

example_use_cases: Joining three consecutive ceremony clips on V1 while keeping background music on A1 and event titles on V2.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Top Bar Undo/Redo buttons alongside multi-track V1/V2/A1 headers with Mute/Lock controls]

articles.title: Adding Overlays & Configuring Blend Modes
articles.goal: Layer celebratory frames, light leaks, or text overlays on upper tracks and blend them naturally using Blend Modes.
prerequisites: A base video clip on V1.
steps: 1. Open the Overlays tab in the Top-Left Asset Dock and search or browse available visual overlays.
2. Click an overlay to place it on an upper track (such as V2) above your main footage.
3. Select the overlay clip and open the Basic tab in the Right-Hand Inspector Panel.
4. Adjust Opacity and choose a Blend Mode (such as Screen for light leaks or Multiply for dark ink textures).
articles.expected_result: The overlay composites smoothly over V1 in the 60fps player according to the chosen Blend Mode.

common_issues.issue: Overlay hides the main video underneath.
common_issues.resolution: Switch the overlay's Blend Mode to Screen or Lighten, or lower Opacity in the Basic Inspector.

example_use_cases: Adding golden sparkler light leaks over a wedding first dance using Screen blend mode.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Overlays dock tab and Basic Inspector Blend Mode selector]

articles.title: Precision Masking & Portrait Retouching
articles.goal: Isolate subjects with geometric or feathered masks, apply subtle portrait retouching, or key out backgrounds.
prerequisites: A video or photo clip selected on the timeline.
steps: 1. Select your clip on the timeline and click the Mask tab in the Right-Hand Inspector Panel.
2. Choose a mask shape (Circle, Rectangle, or Split), then adjust Radius and Feather sliders for soft edges.
3. Switch to the Retouch tab to apply balanced skin smoothing and subtle tone brightening.
4. For green-screen or backdrop replacement, open the Remove BG tab and click Apply Chroma-Key & Backdrop.
articles.expected_result: The Centre 60fps Player renders the feathered mask, portrait retouching, or chroma-keyed backdrop in real time.

common_issues.issue: Mask edge looks too sharp or artificial.
common_issues.resolution: Increase the Feather slider in the Mask Inspector tab until the transition blends naturally.

example_use_cases: Creating a circular picture-in-picture reaction bubble or softening harsh event lighting on a speaker's face.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Inspector Mask and Retouch tabs with live circular feathered mask on canvas]

articles.title: Global Adjustment Layer & Cinematic Lighting
articles.goal: Unify the colour grade across multiple clips using a Global Adjustment Layer and sculpt scene illumination in the Lighting tab.
prerequisites: One or more video clips on the timeline.
steps: 1. Open the Adjustment tab in the Asset Dock to add a Global Adjustment Layer spanning across your timeline clips.
2. Select the Adjustment tab in the Inspector Panel to fine-tune Exposure, Contrast, Saturation, and Colour Temperature.
3. Open the Lighting tab in the Inspector to add cinematic key/fill lighting balance or warm golden-hour highlights.
4. Preview the unified look across clip boundaries in the Centre 60fps Player.
articles.expected_result: All underlying clips inherit a consistent, cohesive colour grade and lighting mood.

common_issues.issue: Colour grade only affects one clip.
common_issues.resolution: Ensure you added a Global Adjustment Layer from the Adjustment dock tab and stretched it over all target clips.

example_use_cases: Matching indoor reception footage with outdoor garden photos using a warm golden-hour colour grade.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Global Adjustment Layer on timeline with Inspector Adjustment and Lighting sliders]

articles.title: Motion Tracking, Keyframe Animation & Speed Curves
articles.goal: Lock callouts or privacy blurs to moving subjects, animate properties with keyframe diamonds, and sculpt speed ramps.
prerequisites: A video clip selected on the timeline.
steps: 1. Open the Tracking tab in the Inspector and click Lock Callout Tracker or Lock Privacy Blur Mask to attach a persistent bounding tracker.
2. Open the Animation tab (or click the <> keyframe diamond next to any Inspector property) at two different playhead timestamps to animate Scale, Position, or Rotation.
3. Open the Speed tab in the Inspector and choose a Speed Curve preset (such as Ease In-Out or Hero Ramp) or adjust the playback multiplier.
articles.expected_result: Tracked boxes follow targets, keyframed properties interpolate smoothly at 60fps, and speed curves vary playback pacing.

common_issues.resolution: Confirm you have added at least two <> keyframe diamonds at different playhead times with different values.

example_use_cases: Blurring a guest's car number plate for privacy or ramping into slow motion as the birthday cake arrives.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Inspector Tracking, Animation keyframe diamonds, and Speed Curve dropdown]

articles.title: Charts & PiP Overlays and Karaoke Captions
articles.goal: Embed picture-in-picture overlays or data charts and generate animated word-by-word Karaoke Captions.
prerequisites: A timeline project with a main video or narration track.
steps: 1. Open the Charts & PiP tab in the Asset Dock to insert a picture-in-picture frame or animated milestone chart onto V2.
2. Open the Captions tab in the Asset Dock and click 💬 Generate Karaoke Captions.
3. Preview the timed, high-contrast captions rendering directly inside the 60fps canvas.
4. Optionally visit AI Avatars to toggle a procedural narrator avatar in the corner of the frame.
articles.expected_result: Charts, PiP layers, and synchronised Karaoke Captions appear crisply over your video with WCAG AA contrast.

common_issues.issue: Captions overlap with a lower-third badge.
common_issues.resolution: Select the lower-third or PiP clip and drag it slightly higher on the canvas using the golden handles.

example_use_cases: Making family history interviews accessible with bold Karaoke Captions for grandparents and social feeds.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Charts & PiP and Captions dock tabs with live Karaoke Captions on #snleMainCanvas]

articles.title: Audio Noise Reduction, Auto-Cut Silence, TTS & Voice Cloning (GDPR Art 9)
articles.goal: Clean up background hiss, strip silent pauses automatically, generate British English TTS voiceovers, and use GDPR Article 9-compliant voice cloning.
prerequisites: An audio or video clip on the timeline (e.g. A1 or V1).
Explicit biometric consent from the speaker before using Voice Cloning.
steps: 1. Select your clip and open the Audio tab in the Right-Hand Inspector Panel.
2. Click Dual-Pass Noise Reduction to suppress room echo, wind, or microphone hiss.
3. Click Auto-Cut Silence to trim dead air between spoken phrases.
4. In the Audio Asset Dock tab, click 🗣 British English Voiceover to synthesise narration.
5. To use Voice Cloning, click Profile & Dub Voice and complete the mandatory GDPR Article 9 explicit biometric consent gate before profiling.
articles.expected_result: Audio sounds crisp and balanced, silent gaps are removed, and biometric voice features remain strictly gated by GDPR Article 9 consent.

common_issues.issue: Voice Cloning button prompts for consent every time.
common_issues.resolution: Biometric voice profiling is Special Category Data under GDPR Article 9 and requires explicit, verified consent before processing.

example_use_cases: Cleaning outdoor party audio and adding a clear British English narration track.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Audio Inspector showing Dual-Pass Noise Reduction, Auto-Cut Silence, and GDPR Art 9 Voice Cloning control]

articles.title: Exporting a 4K Master & Publishing a Reel
articles.goal: Optionally upscale footage with 4K Lanczos-3, render your final composition in-browser, and publish it as a Reel or Master download.
prerequisites: At least one clip on the timeline.
A modern desktop or mobile browser supporting WebCodecs / MediaRecorder.
steps: 1. Review your full timeline from 00:00:00:00 using ▶ Play to verify transitions, captions, and audio levels.
2. Optionally click 4K Lanczos-3 Upscale in the Effects dock tab for sharper detail on older archive footage.
3. Click Export 4K Master in the Top Bar to render your merged timeline directly in the browser with zero server bottleneck.
4. Once rendering completes, download the Master file or click Publish Reel to share directly to your FamilyPlatform or PartyPlatform feed.
articles.expected_result: A high-bitrate 4K Master video is generated locally and ready to download or publish as a Reel.

common_issues.issue: Export takes longer on long multi-track timelines.
common_issues.resolution: Keep the studio tab active and in focus during rendering so the browser does not throttle 60fps canvas capture.

example_use_cases: Exporting a 4K wedding highlight film or publishing a 9:16 family anniversary Reel.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Top Bar Export 4K Master button and Publish Reel completion dialog]

articles.title: Resolving Canvas Playback Stutters & 4K Export Failures
articles.goal: Diagnose and resolve dropped frames during 60fps preview or stalled 4K Master exports.
prerequisites: An active studio session experiencing lag or export interruption.
steps: 1. Pause heavy simultaneous AI overlays (such as 2.5D Parallax + Avatar + Tracking) while rough-cutting on lower-powered devices, then re-enable them before export.
2. Check that your browser tab stays in the foreground during Export 4K Master so requestAnimationFrame is not throttled.
3. Use Undo/Redo if a complex clip stack causes unexpected layout behaviour, or test a shorter 5-second segment first.
4. Ensure your browser is up to date (Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox) with hardware acceleration enabled.
articles.expected_result: Smooth 60fps timeline scrubbing and reliable completion of 4K Master exports.

common_issues.issue: Browser tab backgrounded during export produces a frozen frame.
common_issues.resolution: Keep the Sovereign Video Studio tab visible and awake until the export progress bar reaches 100%.

example_use_cases: Optimising playback performance on a laptop battery before rendering a 3-minute family montage.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: 60fps Player controls and active AI overlay toggles]

articles.title: Fixing Direct R2 Upload Timeouts & Muted Audio Tracks
articles.goal: Recover from Direct R2 upload interruptions and restore sound when a timeline track appears silent.
prerequisites: A media upload error or missing audio during timeline playback.
steps: 1. If a Direct R2 upload times out, check your internet connection and confirm the file size is within your plan limit, then retry.
2. If playback has no sound, inspect the A1 and V1 track headers on the Multi-Track Timeline to verify Mute is not toggled on.
3. Open the Audio tab in the Inspector Panel and check that Clip Volume is above 0%.
4. Verify your device speakers and browser tab are not muted.
articles.expected_result: Uploads complete cleanly to R2 and all unmuted audio tracks play back in sync.

common_issues.issue: Audio plays in preview but is quiet after Auto-Cut Silence.
common_issues.resolution: Click Undo in the Top Bar to restore the pre-cut clip, then adjust the threshold or volume.

example_use_cases: Unmuting an A1 music track that was silenced while recording a voiceover.
screenshots: [INSERT SCREENSHOT: Track header Mute/Lock buttons and Audio Inspector volume slider]
